Petitioners As Accused Nos.1 To 3 Which Is Pending
On The File Of The 1st Acmm, Bangalore.

This Petition, Coming On For Reporting
Settlement, This Day, The Court Made The Following:
 Order
Petitioners-accused Nos.1 to 3 who are sought to be prosecuted for the offence punishable under Section 498-A of IPC and Sections 3 and 4 of the Dowry Prohibition Act, 1961, are before this Court.

2. The case of the prosecution is that, accused No.1 is the husband, accused No.2 is the mother-in-law and accused NC: 2023:KHC:28757 No.3 is the step father-in-law of the defacto complainant and they subjected her to cruelty, both mentally and physically, and also a demand was made to bring money from her parental home.

entities.text: Jai Kumar N vs The State Of Karnataka
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: The parties are present before this Court with their respective counsels and they have filed an application under Section 320(2) and 320(8) r/w Section 482 of Cr.P.C. for compounding of the offence stating that they have amicably settled the matter among themselves in M.C.No.3508/2021 and as per the terms of settlement, marriage of accused No.1 with the defacto complainant has been dissolved mutually and respondent No.2-defacto-complainant has no objection for quashing the impugned proceedings for the offences alleged against the petitioners.
4. The said application is placed on record.

5. Though the offences alleged against the petitioners- accused herein are cognizable and non-compoundable, however, having regard to the fact that the parties have amicably settled the dispute among themselves, it would be a futile exercise, if the petitioners-accused herein are subjected to trial, since the probability of their conviction is remote and bleak in view of the settlement arrived between the parties.
Hence, the continuation of the criminal proceedings will be an abuse of process of law.

Accordingly, I pass the following:
NC: 2023:KHC:28757 ORDER i) Criminal Petition is allowed;
ii) The impugned proceedings in C.C.No.16172/2022 on the file of the 1st Additional Chief Metropolitan Magistrate Court at Bengaluru insofar it relates to petitioners-accused herein stands quashed.
Sd/-
